answer.rationale: Write-path p99 hit 5x about 30 minutes after a release, during a daily settlement peak the platform already expects. That timing is more consistent with a bad build than with ordinary peak load. Rollback previously cleared a checkout spike without customer impact (b1), which is the only inherited case that both matches the trigger and protects writes. Circuit breaking would shed customer writes and violates the objective. Failover and replica routing lack a regional or read-query signal; adding capacity treats load, not a likely regression. Peak-window rollback can still jeopardize in-flight settlement writes, so verify b1 and start with a guarded slice rather than a fleet-wide revert.
